conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with proliferative diabetic retinopathy without macular edema, bilateral

documents.title: Ophthalmology evaluation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Retina and comprehensive ophthalmology, exam date 01/26/2024. Report to primary care.

Reason for visit: Mr. Coleman, 59, with type 2 diabetes for about twenty years and poor control, returns after a long absence; by our records several appointments over the past two years were missed. He describes vision that goes blurry and then clears at different times of day. Faces are hard to make out across a room and colors run together, particularly when the light is low. No pain in the eyes, no light sensitivity, no flashes. He admits he does not take his medicines consistently and has been less active lately.

BP at check-in 142/88.

Best corrected visual acuity: 20/60 OD, 20/70 OS. Pupils equal and reactive, no afferent defect. IOP normal both eyes. Anterior segments quiet; lenses clear for age.
Dilated fundus examination: proliferative diabetic retinopathy in both eyes. No vitreous hemorrhage. No center-involving macular edema on exam or OCT.

Assessment: proliferative diabetic retinopathy OU.
Plan: pan-retinal photocoagulation, right eye first on 02/09, left eye two weeks later. The importance of glucose and blood pressure control and of keeping these appointments was discussed at length with him and his wife.

Medications per patient list. NKDA.
Ophthalmology

documents.title: PRP right eye
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Procedure 02/09/2024: pan-retinal photocoagulation, right eye, topical anesthesia, contact lens, single session. Tolerated well. Left eye scheduled 02/23. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: PRP left eye
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Procedure 02/23/2024: pan-retinal photocoagulation, left eye. Uncomplicated. Follow-up exam both eyes in 3 months to assess regression of neovascularization. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Infectious disease follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic visit 02/26/2024.
HIV RNA not detected (<20). CD4 268, up from 232 in November. This is the first undetectable viral load in our records for him in several years. He credits the blister packs and his sister. Facial molluscum has cleared on exam today.
Plan: stop sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. Continue Biktarvy. Labs every 6 months while stable; next due August.
NKDA.
Infectious Disease

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology, visit 03/20/2024.
IGF-1 205 ng/mL, now within the age-adjusted range on octreotide LAR 20 mg every 4 weeks. No headaches or visual field complaints. Recent laser for diabetic retinopathy noted. Plan: continue the same dose, IGF-1 yearly, repeat pituitary MRI at the next visit if IGF-1 drifts up. Glucose management as per PCP and current insulin.
NKDA.
Endocrinology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: laser to both eyes in February for proliferative retinopathy, says vision is no worse, still blurry in dim light. HIV undetectable in Feb, SMX-TMP stopped. IGF-1 normal at endocrine. Feels himself, working full routes.
On glargine 24 and lispro when he remembers. Fasting sugars 140-200 on his meter.

Exam: BP above goal. Skin clear, no residual papules on face or neck. Lungs clear, heart regular, trace ankle edema. Feet intact, insensate as before.

A/P: molluscum resolved, off the list. CKD 5 not on dialysis, BMP today; nephrology visit in June. T2DM above goal, A1c today, he declines changes to insulin again. HTN above goal on lisinopril 10; he would like one more stretch of salt restriction, recheck next visit. PDR s/p PRP, ophtho follow-up in May. HIV per ID.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Nephrology, visit 06/19/2024.
CKD stage 5 from diabetic nephropathy, eGFR about 11, no uremic symptoms reported today. Volume acceptable. PTH remains elevated on calcitriol; phosphorus near goal on sevelamer.
We spent most of the visit on kidney replacement options. He and his wife attended our dialysis education session last month. He prefers in-center hemodialysis when the time comes.
Plan: labs every 2 months, see us in 6 months or sooner if symptoms. Continue current medications.
NKDA.
Nephrology

documents.title: Question about dialysis
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is his wife writing from Lamar's account. The kidney doctor talked about dialysis last week. He says he is fine and doesn't want to think about it. Is there anything we should be doing now to get ready? He is still working every day.

documents.title: RE: Question about dialysis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for writing. The most useful things right now are keeping the labs nephrology asks for, sticking with the sevelamer at meals, limiting salt and potassium-heavy foods, and calling if he notices nausea, itching, more swelling or getting short of breath. Nephrology will decide timing with him. I am glad you went to the education session together. Happy to talk it through at his next visit.

events.reason: Right foot swelling and shape change

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: right foot swelling and deformity, insensate foot

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wife made this appointment. She has been watching his right foot get bigger and change shape over the spring and summer; he says it doesn't hurt much and he has kept working. Boots fit badly on that side now. No fever. No open sores that he knows of.

Exam: afebrile. Right midfoot visibly swollen and warm to the touch compared with the left, shape abnormal through the arch. Skin intact, no ulcer, no drainage. Left foot unremarkable. Both feet insensate to monofilament.

A/P: warm swollen deformed foot in a man with dense neuropathy, concerning for Charcot arthropathy. Called orthopedics, they will see him on 9/11 and image there. Until then: off the foot as much as possible, no long walking shifts; work note given. Return immediately for fever, redness spreading or any skin break.
Rest of chronic issues deferred to next routine visit.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic neuropathic arthropathy
conditions.note: Charcot neuroarthropathy, right foot and ankle

reports.text: Right foot, three views, weight-bearing as tolerated. Fragmentation of bone at the midfoot articulations with subluxation of the joints and surrounding sclerosis. Soft-tissue swelling over the midfoot. No soft-tissue gas. No radiopaque foreign body.
reports.conclusion: Advanced destructive change of the right midfoot joints with fragmentation, subluxation and sclerosis.

documents.title: Orthopedic foot and ankle consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Foot and ankle clinic, visit 09/11/2024. Letter to PCP.

History: Mr. Coleman, 59, has had about 8 months of slowly progressive swelling and change in shape of the right foot. He says the foot is changing shape and that he sometimes hears a cracking or grinding when he walks, with little or no discomfort. Around nine months ago he rolled the ankle on a broken sidewalk and carried on with his deliveries because it barely hurt. The swelling has crept up since then and the foot now looks crooked to him. His wife has noticed an odd gait, though he never complains of pain. Peripheral neuropathy for about five years. He spends long days standing and walking for work, usually in an old pair of boots. No fevers, chills or recent infections; review of systems otherwise negative.

Exam: right foot markedly swollen, warm and red, with collapse of the midfoot and obvious deformity. Joint instability and bony crepitus on palpation; active motion reduced. Ankle reflexes absent on both sides. DP and PT pulses 2+ bilaterally. Skin intact. Left foot normal.

Labs: white count normal, ESR and CRP normal.
X-rays right foot: bone fragmentation, joint subluxation and sclerosis, advanced joint destruction.
No joint aspiration, as there is nothing to suggest infection.

Impression: Charcot neuroarthropathy of the right foot and ankle, active phase.
Plan: total contact cast today, changed weekly here; non-weight-bearing as much as he can manage with a knee scooter. Once the foot has consolidated, I would plan a right ankle arthrodesis to give him a stable plantigrade foot. Work note for no standing work.

Medications: as on PCP list. NKDA.
Orthopedics

documents.title: Flu and COVID
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Arrived on knee scooter, right leg in a cast. Influenza and 2024-25 COVID given, one in each arm. Cast intact, no rubbing at the top edge, he has ortho cast changes weekly. Reminded about AWV in November.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
The year: retinopathy lasered in Feb. HIV suppressed. Right Charcot foot found in September, in a total contact cast since, changed weekly at ortho, plan for ankle fusion later. Not doing deliveries while in the cast, per ortho. Kidney function close to dialysis; nephrology in December.
Function: uses knee scooter, wife drives him. Independent with dressing and bathing using a shower chair. No falls. Memory: sister and wife both say he is sharp now.
PHQ-2 1. Feels frustrated being off the route but not down.
HCP on file.

Exam: BP above goal. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Left foot intact, insensate. Right leg in cast, skin at cast edges intact, toes warm.

Prevention: Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months. Flu and COVID done in October. Colonoscopy next 2029.
Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c.
RTC after nephrology visit.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Nephrology, visit 12/11/2024.
eGFR about 9. Fatigue is clearly worse over the last two months; he is sleeping more and struggling to get through the day even off work. No pericardial rub, no asterixis.
We agreed it is time to start hemodialysis. Plan: tunneled hemodialysis catheter by interventional radiology the week of 01/13, first in-center treatment the same week, three sessions weekly at our outpatient unit. Epoetin will be given with treatments once he starts. Continue calcitriol, sevelamer and his other medications.
NKDA.
Nephrology

documents.title: Tunneled hemodialysis catheter placement
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Interventional radiology procedure report, 01/13/2025.
Indication: end-stage renal disease, initiation of hemodialysis.
Procedure: ultrasound-guided access of the right internal jugular vein, patent and compressible. Tunneled cuffed hemodialysis catheter placed under fluoroscopy with the tip at the cavoatrial junction. Both lumens aspirate and flush well, locked with heparin. Moderate sedation. No complications, no pneumothorax on post-procedure fluoroscopy. Catheter ready for use today.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Dialysis unit admission summary
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body: Outpatient dialysis unit, initial treatment summary. First hemodialysis 01/13/2025 via right IJ tunneled catheter, uneventful. Schedule Monday/Wednesday/Friday mornings. Epoetin alfa 4000 units IV each treatment started for anemia of CKD. Calcitriol and sevelamer continued. Target weight to be set over the first weeks. Monthly labs will be faxed to the PCP.

documents.title: Post-dialysis start check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check in after his first week and a half of dialysis. Wife answered, he was napping after the morning run. Washed out after sessions but otherwise ok, catheter site dry. Unit is managing epoetin. Moved his PCP follow-up to a Thursday so it doesn't collide with treatments. Med list updated with dialysis unit summary.

documents.title: Infectious disease follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic, visit 02/20/2025.
Viral load 1,850 copies/mL after being undetectable last year; CD4 241. He acknowledges that with the move to dialysis three mornings a week his routine fell apart, and he has missed several doses each week. Sister had stepped back once things were going well.
Plan: continue Biktarvy; doses to be taken at the same time every evening, sister back to checking the blister pack, pharmacy auto-refill confirmed. Repeat viral load in 3 months.
NKDA.
Infectious Disease

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit since starting HD 1/13 (MWF mornings, right IJ tunneled catheter). Tired after treatments, better the next day. Unit labs reviewed from the faxes. Epoetin with treatments.
ID: viral load back up to 1,850 last month with missed doses around the dialysis change. Sister checking packs again.
Foot still in cast, weekly changes, ortho thinks it is cooling down.
Sugars: lower fasting numbers on dialysis days, no lows below 70.

Exam: BP above goal. Catheter dressing clean and dry. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Trace edema left ankle. Right leg cast intact.

A/P
ESRD on HD: per nephrology/unit. Labs come from the unit, so only A1c drawn here.
T2DM: A1c today, watch for hypoglycemia now that he is on dialysis; told him to call with any reading under 70.
HIV: adherence back on track per sister.
HTN: unit adjusting target weight, will reassess.
Shingrix #2 today, series complete.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology, visit 04/16/2025.
Now on hemodialysis since January. IGF-1 198 ng/mL, within range on octreotide LAR 20 mg monthly. No headaches or visual change beyond his known retinopathy. Injection days have been moved to Tuesdays so they do not land on dialysis days. Continue. IGF-1 in a year.
NKDA.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Foot and ankle follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Foot and ankle clinic, 05/21/2025.
After eight months in a total contact cast the right foot is cooler and the swelling is down. Moving him into a CROW walker today with gradual return to protected weight-bearing. Skin intact.
The right ankle arthrodesis remains the plan once the foot has fully consolidated. Not scheduled yet; we will need medical clearance given his dialysis and other conditions.
No return to delivery work for now.
NKDA.
Orthopedics

conditions.label: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food
medications.reason: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, started at discharge

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Right internal jugular tunneled catheter with tip at the cavoatrial junction. The cardiac silhouette is enlarged. Pulmonary vascular congestion with interstitial edema bilaterally. No large pleural effusion. No pneumothorax.

Left ventricular cavity size normal. Global hypokinesis, no regional pattern. Estimated LVEF 30% by biplane method. Right ventricular size and function normal. No significant valvular stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 30% with global hypokinesis. No significant valve disease.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department record, 07/14/2025, received 07/18/2025.

CC: shortness of breath.
HPI: 60-year-old man on hemodialysis for ESRD (nephrology-managed), with diabetes and HIV, here with two days of steadily worsening breathlessness. Has to sleep propped up, and his legs have swelled again. He says he has been eating saltier food over the holiday week and missed several doses of his pills.
Meds per list: Biktarvy, insulin glargine, lispro scale, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, sevelamer, calcitriol, octreotide LAR monthly, epoetin with dialysis. NKDA.

Vitals on arrival: BP 160/90, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 90% on room air.
Exam: crackles halfway up both lung fields. S3 gallop. JVP elevated. 2+ pitting edema to the mid-shins. Catheter site clean.
Labs: Na 138, K 4.9, BNP 900.
CXR: cardiomegaly with pulmonary congestion.

Course: placed on 2 L nasal cannula with improvement. Nephrology consulted for urgent ultrafiltration. Admitted to medicine with telemetry.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admission 07/14/2025 - 07/17/2025, regional hospital medicine service.
Principal diagnosis: acute heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, new.
Course: urgent hemodialysis with ultrafiltration on admission night and again 07/16, with fluid removal; off oxygen by day 2. Echo: LVEF 30% with global hypokinesis, no significant valve disease. Ischemic evaluation deferred to outpatient cardiology. Lisinopril continued. Started carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, tolerated with HR in the 80s.
Discharge weight to be used as new dialysis target, communicated to his unit.
Discharge medications: carvedilol 6.25 mg BID (new), Biktarvy daily, insulin glargine 24 units qhs, lispro scale, lisinopril 10 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, sevelamer 800 mg TID with meals, calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily, octreotide LAR 20 mg monthly, epoetin with dialysis.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, cardiology 6-8 weeks, resume regular dialysis schedule 07/18.
Allergies: NKDA.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food
medications.reason: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharged 7/17 after 3 days for new HFrEF with volume overload (EF 30%). Discharge summary and ED record reviewed. Interactive contact by RN on 7/18.
Feels back to normal breathing, sleeps flat again. Back on MWF dialysis, unit lowered his target weight. Taking carvedilol twice a day, no dizziness.
Honest that the holiday salt and skipped pills set this off. Wife has thrown out the soy sauce.

Exam: HR in the 70s, BP above goal. No JVD at 45 degrees. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no gallop heard today. Trace ankle edema left; right in CROW walker. Catheter site clean.

A/P
HFrEF, new: tolerating carvedilol, HR and BP allow titration. Increase carvedilol to 12.5 mg BID. Continue lisinopril 10. Daily weights at home, call for gain over 2 kg between sessions. Cardiology referral placed, outpatient ischemic evaluation to be discussed there.
ESRD: per unit, weight targets as discharged.
HTN: should improve on carvedilol.
Med reconciliation done, list updated.
RTC 3 months, sooner if symptoms.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outpatient cardiology, 09/17/2025. Letter to PCP.

Referred after a July admission for decompensated heart failure, LVEF 30% with global hypokinesis. On hemodialysis since January. Since discharge he has been free of orthopnea and his weights have stayed near target with his dialysis sessions. Can walk a block in his walker before he needs to stop, limited more by the foot than breath. NYHA class II.

BP 136/82. JVP not elevated. Lungs clear. Regular rhythm, no gallop. No significant edema.

Assessment: HFrEF, euvolemic on current dialysis prescription.
Plan: continue carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg. Given diabetes and family history, I offered an ischemic evaluation; he would like to hold off for now and revisit at his next visit. Return in 6 months, sooner for symptoms.

Medications reviewed. NKDA.
Cardiology

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thursday, non-dialysis day. Influenza L deltoid, COVID R deltoid, RSV L deltoid lower, per PCP order (age 60 with ESRD and heart failure). Each VIS given. Sat for 15 min, no issues. Wife drove.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Year in review: HD since January via tunneled catheter. HFrEF admission in July, stable since on carvedilol 12.5 BID, saw cardiology in September and chose to wait on ischemic testing. Charcot foot now in a CROW walker; ankle fusion still on ortho's list for when the foot is ready. Octreotide continues, IGF-1 normal in April. HIV labs with ID.
Function: walks household distances in the walker. Wife drives. Independent in self care. No falls this year. Memory fine per wife.
PHQ-2 0.
Advance care planning: reviewed HCP; he would want dialysis continued and full treatment; documented.

Exam: BP a little above goal, better than last year. Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema. Left foot intact, insensate; right in CROW. Catheter site clean.

Prevention: flu, COVID and RSV done in October. Shingrix complete. Colonoscopy due 2029. Lipids and A1c today.
RTC 2 months.
